newsitem.title: GERMANY: PreussenElektra denies Russian power talks.
newsitem.headline: PreussenElektra denies Russian power talks.

text.p: German electricity supplier PreussenElektra on Monday denied that it is involved in secret negotiations with the Russian government about the construction of an electricity network.
The group, which is a unit of the German diversified utility group Veba AG, was involved in discussions about a trans-European network, Josef Nelles, spokesman for PreussenElektra, said.
He added that this discussion was taking place at company level.
The German newspaper Welt am Sonntag said on Sunday that PreussenElektra was talking to the Russian government about delivering electricity to Russia.
The newspaper report said the proposed power line would start east of the Urals and cross Poland into Germany.
Nelles said that it was also untrue that Russia wanted to sell around 4,000 megawatts of power a year.

The spokesman said that any east-west high-grade network would require billions of marks in investment, which would require bringing Poland, White Russia and the Baltic States together "under one hat", PreussenElektra said.
The group would not comment on a price per kilowatt hour of three to four pfennigs, mentioned in the Welt am Sonntag story.
It was technically possible nowadays to build an electricity grid which can transport around 4,000 megawatts annually, Nelles said.
In order to further develop technological possibilities, a request has been made to the European Union to carry out a six-million mark feasability study on the idea of a transeuropean network.
